cards.title: Plume: Scaffolding Text Composition in Dashboards
cards.relevant_page_map: motivation pp. 2–4; formative basis pp. 5–8; interface pp. 9–12; evaluation pp. 12–15; limitations pp. 15–16.

identity_entries.value: motivation pp. 2–4; formative basis pp. 5–8; interface pp. 9–12; evaluation pp. 12–15; limitations pp. 15–16.
quotes: "Despite text being an indispensable component of visualization dashboards [66], most popular visualization and dashboard tools lack features to aid authors in composing text." (p. 2)
"Based on our formative work, we present our findings as a set of themes that summarize our codebook and serve as design considerations for Plume." (p. 8)

"In this section, we describe the system design of Plume by tracing the importance of the dashboard tree for surfacing a coherent reading order for the author, offering suggestions for meaningful placement of text in the dashboard, as well as identifying relevant context for generating new text using LLMs." (p. 9)
"We conducted remote user sessions with dashboard creators to evaluate the utility of our proposed workflow for authoring dashboard text and identify useful directions for future work." (p. 12)

"While our user study provided valuable insights into dashboard authors’ initial impressions of Plume, as well as their attitudes and trust toward generative AI in dashboard text, it is crucial to explore its impact on longer-term workflows [24]." (p. 15)

entries.value: dashboard text composition and updating were tedious, unstructured, and poorly supported (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "Previous research has highlighted that the process of composing and updating text in dashboards is seen as tedious and unstructured." (p. 2)

entries.value: M2
author_claim — the paper describes and qualitatively evaluates the workflow without isolating this mechanism experimentally.
paper_reports_prior_practice — the introduction synthesizes prior reports of dashboard text work.
ambiguous placement could leave authors or viewers inspecting multiple charts to infer which visualization a text fragment describes (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "As a result, the viewer must carefully read the text and examine both charts, making it more difficult to quickly grasp the relationship between the text and the visual data, reducing overall clarity." (p. 8)

entries.value: authors place content within visible nested frames and hover over text to inspect its descendant context (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "When hovering over a piece of text with a cursor, Plume additionally highlights direct descendants of that frame, making it particularly noticeable what the text in question is referring to." (p. 9)

entries.value: M1
author_claim — the change is demonstrated in the interface and argued from the design, not tested against an alternative layout.
paper_reports_prior_practice — the formative dashboard corpus supplies the ambiguous-placement example.
authors could face “blank canvas paralysis” when starting dashboard prose from scratch (PDF p. 13).
quotes: "They appreciated its ability to quickly generate relevant text, overcoming the challenges associated with text authoring, such as ‘blank canvas paralysis,’ where users struggle to start writing from scratch." (p. 13)

entries.value: authors generate a draft, inspect role-specific recommendations and metrics, then manually rewrite it or invoke regenerate, shorten, or simplify (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "Based on the selected text role, Plume provides recommendations for how to approach the writing of such text as well as surfaces text metrics. The user may then either manually rewrite the text or use Plume to re-generate, shorten, or simplify their text to ensure that it is readable at the level appropriate for their audience." (p. 11)

entries.value: author_claim — participants described the combined workflow as a useful starting point, but no component contrast was run.
paper_reports_prior_practice — participant accounts establish the difficulty of beginning from scratch.

rq3_entries.value: Plume proposes which kinds of text to add and where, evaluates selected snippets against role-specific criteria, and generates candidate wording with an LLM (PDF pp. 10–11).
quotes: "Once the author completes the dashboard layout and adds visualizations to relevant frames, Plume provides dynamic feedback and recommendations for authoring text." (p. 10)
"The system generates text by sending a prompt to a large language model (LLM)." (p. 11)

rq3_entries.value: the author supplies otherwise unavailable context, seeds communication goal and tone through accepted or locked text, and remains responsible for accuracy and review (PDF pp. 12, 15).
quotes: "Since the author had actively written or accepted this text, such text can serve as an indicator of the communication goal of the dashboard, any external context not otherwise inferred from the data that the author would like to add, as well as tone and phrasing." (p. 12)
"Participants suggested that notifications for updates could help ensure that authors maintain control over the accuracy of the text." (p. 15)

rq3_entries.value: not_measured — the study elicited usability, workflow impressions, and action patterns rather than learning or transfer.
author_raised — participants resisted unreviewed AI generation because dynamic text could be inaccurate (PDF p. 15).
quotes: "While Plume’s ability to generate text based on connected data was seen as a major advantage, as discussed before, concerns about inaccuracies within these dynamic updates reflect participants’ hesitation to blindly let AI generate all of their dashboard text." (p. 15)

rq3_entries.value: no — support remains available and does not withdraw as competence grows.
authors must vet generated text, preserve intended meaning, and decide when updates are accurate enough to accept; the paper describes no reduction in this responsibility (PDF p. 15).
quotes: "The potential for stale or misleading text due to automatic updates was a concern across multiple participants, prompting a need for mechanisms that provide notifications for updates or a review process before changes go live." (p. 15)
"Participant sessions were approximately one hour long and entailed three segments." (p. 12)

claim_entries.value: the paper claims that Plume's proposed dashboard-text workflow is flexible, fast, and effective (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "Findings suggest that Plume’s proposed workflow is flexible, fast, and effective, and inform a number of opportunities for follow-up research." (p. 12)

claim_entries.value: performance — the headline language concerns workflow speed and effectiveness (PDF p. 13).
quotes: "Participants, in general, found Plume to be fast and efficient in helping them generate text relevant for their typical work tasks." (p. 13)

claim_entries.value: empirical — the focal claim is supported through sessions with dashboard creators (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "We conducted remote user sessions with dashboard creators to evaluate the utility of our proposed workflow for authoring dashboard text and identify useful directions for future work." (p. 12)

claim_entries.value: single_condition_usability — participants used Plume in one open-ended authoring condition and reported impressions (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "Participants had the opportunity to use Plume in an open-ended authoring task and shared usage impressions and suggestions for future improvement." (p. 12)
"For the main study, we recruited 12 professionals (𝑃1 − 𝑃12) with dashboard creation experience from relevant community channels." (p. 12)

claim_entries.value: target_practitioners — experienced dashboard authors from data-analysis, consulting, and management roles (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "Participants had, on average, 8.5 years of experience in dashboard authoring (min. 4 years, max. 18 years) and a diverse range of backgrounds, from data analysts and consultants to data-relevant team management roles." (p. 12)

claim_entries.value: none — the study included no control, baseline system, ablation, or pre/post comparison.
descriptive_only — the paper reports SUS and action-log means, standard deviations, minima, and maxima without inferential tests (PDF p. 14).
quotes: "Participants’ action log analysis revealed that they accepted, on average, 66.1% of snippets created by Plume as-is (SD 21.4%, min 20.0%, max 88.2%)." (p. 14)

claim_entries.value: approximately one hour — including an authoring task of up to 20 minutes (PDF pp. 12–13).
quotes: "Participant sessions were approximately one hour long and entailed three segments." (p. 12)
"They were then given a dashboard authoring task and up to 20 minutes to complete this task using Plume while thinking aloud." (p. 13)

claim_entries.value: generated prose was often too verbose, while automatic updates raised stale-text and accuracy concerns (PDF p. 15).
quotes: "Participants often found the text generated by Plume more verbose than they intended." (p. 15)

"The potential for stale or misleading text due to automatic updates was a concern across multiple participants, prompting a need for mechanisms that provide notifications for updates or a review process before changes go live." (p. 15)

claim_entries.value: “flexible, fast, and effective” exceeds a single-session, single-condition first-impressions study; the authors themselves call longitudinal real-world observation essential (PDF pp. 12, 15).
quotes: "The primary goal of our evaluation was to elicit professional dashboard authors’ first impressions on Plume’s proposed workflow of authoring text." (p. 12)

"Longitudinal studies would be essential to observe more complex insights about how Plume is integrated into existing workflows: how trust in generated text evolves over time, how Plume influences dashboard creation in real-world settings, and which types of dashboards benefit most—or least—from this assistance." (p. 15)

paper_code_entries.value: dashboard text authoring and data-driven communication (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "To address this gap, we developed Plume, a system designed to help dashboard authors write text for their visualizations by considering the diverse roles that text plays." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support helps authors produce and refine dashboard prose in the current task (PDF p. 13).
quotes: "This speed in generating initial text provided users with a strong starting point for refinement, reducing the time spent on the aspects of text authoring they typically find tedious." (p. 13)

paper_code_entries.value: expert_or_professional — the evaluated users were experienced practitioners (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "Participants had, on average, 8.5 years of experience in dashboard authoring (min. 4 years, max. 18 years) and a diverse range of backgrounds, from data analysts and consultants to data-relevant team management roles." (p. 12)

paper_code_entries.value: execution_or_skill_gap — authors could know their data and charts yet struggle to begin expressing them in dashboard prose (PDF p. 13).
quotes: "They appreciated its ability to quickly generate relevant text, overcoming the challenges associated with text authoring, such as ‘blank canvas paralysis,’ where users struggle to start writing from scratch." (p. 13)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the evaluation analyzed authoring actions and use patterns rather than learning or transfer (PDF p. 13).
quotes: "Text authoring actions with Plume—such as creation, editing, generation, refinement, or deletion of text snippets—were also logged and analyzed to uncover use patterns." (p. 13)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the sidebar organizes text authoring into semantic-role suggestions with recommended locations (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "Dashboard-level guidance consists of a series of suggestions surfaced in the sidebar (panel C in Figure 1) that recommend what text may be useful in the dashboard and where it should be placed." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — feedback changes with the selected text role and the current snippet's metrics (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "Based on the selected text role, Plume provides recommendations for how to approach the writing of such text as well as surfaces text metrics." (p. 11)

paper_code_entries.value: adaptation — generation context changes with text role and position in the current dashboard (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "Lastly, the context required by the prompt again depends on the text role and the position of the text in the dashboard frames." (p. 12)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_or_foundation_model — an LLM produces the generated dashboard text (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "We use OpenAI’s ChatGPT 4o LLM to generate text." (p. 12)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — the scaffold's generated meaning comes from ChatGPT 4o (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "We use OpenAI’s ChatGPT 4o LLM to generate text." (p. 12)

limitations: "Participants often found the text generated by Plume more verbose than they intended." (p. 15)

"The potential for stale or misleading text due to automatic updates was a concern across multiple participants, prompting a need for mechanisms that provide notifications for updates or a review process before changes go live." (p. 15)

"While our user study provided valuable insights into dashboard authors’ initial impressions of Plume, as well as their attitudes and trust toward generative AI in dashboard text, it is crucial to explore its impact on longer-term workflows [24]." (p. 15)
"However, there are still opportunities to enhance the coherence of the generated content." (p. 15)
boundary_conditions: "Participant sessions were approximately one hour long and entailed three segments." (p. 12)

"While all participants in our study were experienced dashboard authors, they speculated that novice users might find the most value in assistance with generating initial ideas and establishing their unique voice." (p. 15)

"For instance, although we tested our system to confirm that it performs well on common Vega-Lite charts (our evaluations used line charts with and without uncertainty bands, bar charts, scatter plots, and area charts), computational frameworks specifically fine-tuned for extracting insights based on the data [69, 74] could be added in a modular way, improving the insight text generation in general and for more complex chart types in particular." (p. 15)
